I have sufficient data. Here are my findings for Home Depot (HD).

## Home Depot — FY2023–FY2025 (fiscal year = calendar year in which FY ends)

| Fiscal Year | Period | Revenue ($B) | Net Income ($B) | Net Margin | Gross Margin | Operating Margin | Rev. Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2023 | 2022-01-31 → 2023-01-29 | 157.403 | 17.105 | **10.9%** | 33.5% | 15.3% | +4.1% |
| FY2024 | 2023-01-30 → 2024-01-28 | 152.669 | 15.143 | **9.9%** | 33.4% | 14.2% | −3.0% |
| FY2025 | 2024-01-29 → 2025-02-02 | 159.514 | 14.806 | **9.3%** | 33.4% | 13.5% | +4.5% |

All figures from [HD-10K-FY2023], [HD-10K-FY2024], [HD-10K-FY2025]. Net margins are the server-computed values (net_income / revenue).

**Key observations:**
- Revenue dipped in FY2024 (−3.0%) then recovered to a record $159.5B in FY2025 (+4.5%) [HD-10K-FY2024], [HD-10K-FY2025].
- Net income declined every year: $17.105B → $15.143B → $14.806B, so net margin compressed steadily from 10.9% to 9.3% — a cumulative decline of 1.6 percentage points, with no year of margin expansion.
- Gross margin was essentially flat (33.5% → 33.4% → 33.4%), so the margin erosion came from below the gross-profit line: operating margin fell 15.3% → 14.2% → 13.5%.

**Margin drivers cited in the filings:**
- **FY2024 (fiscal 2023):** Gross profit fell $1.8B (−3.4%) to $51.0B; gross margin 33.4% vs 33.5% prior year, "primarily reflects price stabilization as well as reduction and optimization of our inventory position, partially offset by lower supply chain costs"; shrink pressure eased through the year [HD-10K-FY2024#p200]. Diluted EPS fell to $15.11 from $16.69, "primarily driven by lower net earnings" [HD-10K-FY2024#p204].
- **FY2025 (fiscal 2024):** Gross profit rose $2.3B (+4.6%) to $53.3B; gross margin held at 33.4%, reflecting "lower transportation costs and lower shrink within our Primary segment, offset by the inclusion of SRS in our consolidated results" [HD-10K-FY2025#p201]. The margin squeeze came from operating expenses: SG&A rose $2.2B (+8.1%) to $28.7B, or 18.0% of net sales vs 17.4%, "primarily reflects higher payroll costs, deleverage from a negative comparable sales environment and lower legal-related benefits"; D&A rose 13.5% to $3.0B (1.9% of sales vs 1.8%), including $239M of added intangible amortization, $218M of it from SRS [HD-10K-FY2025#p202].

**Bottom line for the comparison:** HD's net margin is not stable — it fell monotonically from 10.9% (FY2023) to 9.3% (FY2025), a 1.6 pt decline, driven by SG&A deleverage, payroll costs, and SRS acquisition dilution rather than gross-margin deterioration.

## Lowe's (LOW) — FY2023–FY2025

**Note on fiscal year convention:** Lowe's fiscal years end in late January/early February. Per the tool's convention (fiscal_year = calendar year in which the fiscal year ends), FY2023 ended 2023-02-03, FY2024 ended 2024-02-02, and FY2025 ended 2025-01-31.

| Fiscal Year | Period | Revenue ($B) | Net Income ($B) | Net Margin | Gross Margin | Operating Margin | Rev. Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2023 | 2022-01-29 → 2023-02-03 | 97.059 | 6.437 | **6.6%** | 33.2% | 10.5% | +0.8% |
| FY2024 | 2023-02-04 → 2024-02-02 | 86.377 | 7.726 | **8.9%** | 33.4% | 13.4% | −11.0% |
| FY2025 | 2024-02-03 → 2025-01-31 | 83.674 | 6.957 | **8.3%** | 33.3% | 12.5% | −3.1% |

Sources: [LOW-10K-FY2023], [LOW-10K-FY2024], [LOW-10K-FY2025]

**Net margin range:** 6.6% → 8.9% → 8.3%; spread of 2.3 percentage points across the three years, with a 2.3 pt jump in FY2024 and a 0.6 pt decline in FY2025. Gross margin was remarkably flat (33.2% / 33.4% / 33.3%, a 0.2 pt range); the net-margin swing came from below the gross-margin line (SG&A leverage and one-time items).

### Margin drivers per the 10-Ks

**FY2024 (fiscal 2023, year ended 2024-02-02) — margin expanded despite an 11% sales decline:**
- Gross margin leveraged 16 bps vs. the prior year, driven by productivity initiatives and lower transportation costs, partly offset by higher costs from supply-chain network expansion [LOW-10K-FY2024#p158, #p159].
- SG&A leveraged 292 bps as a percentage of sales, primarily from cycling the prior-year long-lived asset impairment, loss on sale and closing costs on the Canadian retail business sale, plus two favorable legal settlements in the current year — partly offset by fixed-cost deleverage on lower sales [LOW-10K-FY2024#p159]. This SG&A swing is the main reason net margin jumped to 8.9% even as revenue fell 11%.
- Sales weakness: comparable sales fell in 12 of 14 product categories, with DIY discretionary/big-ticket demand soft and Lumber pressured by commodity deflation [LOW-10K-FY2024#p158].

**FY2025 (fiscal 2024, year ended 2025-01-31) — margin gave back some ground:**
- Net sales fell 3.1% to $83.7B on a 2.7% comparable sales decline (3.0% fewer transactions, +0.3% average ticket) [LOW-10K-FY2025#p166].
- Gross margin decreased 7 bps, primarily from supply-chain investments, partly offset by productivity initiatives [LOW-10K-FY2025#p167].
- SG&A deleveraged 72 bps, driven by employee compensation and benefits (higher bonus attainment, higher employee insurance costs) and by cycling the prior year's favorable legal settlements; D&A deleveraged 8 bps [LOW-10K-FY2025#p167]. These explain the net margin decline from 8.9% to 8.3%.

**FY2023 (fiscal 2022, year ended 2023-02-03) — baseline year:**
- Gross margin contracted 7 bps vs. FY2022, hurt by 30 bps from higher transportation costs and supply-chain network expansion and 20 bps from inventory-related items [LOW-10K-FY2023#p157].
- Revenue was roughly flat (+0.8%) at $97.1B, the highest of the three years; net margin of 6.6% was the lowest of the three, reflecting the absence of the FY2024 SG&A benefits (the Canadian business impairment/sale costs hit the prior year, and the favorable legal settlements came in FY2024) [LOW-10K-FY2024#p159].

**Summary for the comparison:** Lowe's net margin was 6.6% (FY2023), 8.9% (FY2024), 8.3% (FY2025) — a 2.3 pt range — while gross margin was essentially flat at ~33.3%. Revenue declined sharply over the period ($97.1B → $86.4B → $83.7B). The margin volatility is driven by SG&A items (legal settlements, Canadian business exit costs, bonus/insurance costs) rather than by gross margin.

Intel's FY2024 net loss was **$18.756B** (net margin −35.3%) on revenue of $53.101B, down 2.1% year over year [INTC-10K-FY2024]. Operating loss was $11.678B (operating margin −22.0%), with gross margin falling to 32.7% from 40.0% in FY2023 [INTC-10K-FY2024].

Per the 10-K, the loss was driven mainly by large non-cash and restructuring charges:

- **$9.9B non-cash charge to provision for income taxes**, substantially related to valuation allowances recorded against net deferred tax assets — this is the single largest driver of the gap between the $11.7B operating loss and the $18.8B net loss [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103].
- **$3.3B of charges**, substantially all in cost of sales, for non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation of manufacturing assets, a substantial majority tied to the Intel 7 process node [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103].
- **$3.1B of non-cash goodwill and acquired intangible asset impairments** for certain reporting units [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103][INTC-10K-FY2024#p170].
- **$2.8B of restructuring charges** under the 2024 Restructuring Plan announced in Q3 2024, aimed at cutting headcount (~15% reduction in core Intel workforce by early 2025), operating expenses and capex; total expected charges are ~$3.0B [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103][INTC-10K-FY2024#p476]. This includes $442M of impairments on construction-in-progress assets from exiting/outsourcing internal test hardware manufacturing and $103M on leased assets and leasehold improvements from real estate exits [INTC-10K-FY2024#p170].

So the loss reflects a combination of weak gross margin, manufacturing asset write-downs and accelerated depreciation, goodwill impairment, restructuring, and a very large deferred-tax valuation allowance.

Intel's FY2024 10-K attributes the large loss mainly to four big, mostly non-cash charges, plus a modest revenue decline [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103]:

1. **Restructuring — $2.8 billion** under the 2024 Restructuring Plan (announced Q3 2024), targeting ~15% workforce reduction [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103][INTC-10K-FY2024#p476].
2. **Manufacturing asset impairments / accelerated depreciation — $3.3 billion**, substantially all in cost of sales, mostly tied to the Intel 7 process node; this drove the gross-margin drop from 40.0% to 32.7% [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103].
3. **Goodwill and acquired intangible impairments — $3.1 billion** non-cash [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103][INTC-10K-FY2024#p170].
4. **Tax valuation allowance — $9.9 billion** non-cash, based on a three-year cumulative historical loss position as of Q3 2024 [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103][INTC-10K-FY2024#p482].

### Key figures (USD billions) [INTC-10K-FY2024]

|---|---|---|

| Net margin | -35.3% | 3.1% |
| R&D | 16.546 (31.2% of revenue) | 16.046 (29.6%) |
| Revenue growth | -2.1% | -14.0% |

### 10-K explanation of the FY2024 loss
The 10-K attributes the loss to four large, mostly non-cash charges plus a modest revenue decline [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103]:

1. **Restructuring — $2.8 billion** in charges from the **2024 Restructuring Plan** (announced Q3 2024), targeting an approximate **15% reduction in core Intel workforce** by early 2025; total expected charges ~$3.0 billion, cumulative cost $2.8 billion as of Dec 28, 2024 [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103][INTC-10K-FY2024#p476].
2. **Manufacturing asset impairments / accelerated depreciation — $3.3 billion**, "substantially all of which were recorded to cost of sales," related to non-cash impairments and acceleration of depreciation for certain manufacturing assets, "a substantial majority of which related to our **Intel 7 process node**" [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103]. This is the main driver of the gross-margin collapse from 40.0% to 32.7%.
3. **Goodwill and acquired intangible impairments — $3.1 billion** non-cash, for certain reporting units and acquired intangibles [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103][INTC-10K-FY2024#p170].
4. **Tax valuation allowance — $9.9 billion** non-cash charge to provision for income taxes, "substantially related to valuation allowances recorded to our net deferred tax assets" [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103][INTC-10K-FY2024#p104]. The 10-K explains the company determined in Q3 2024 it was "more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be recoverable based upon our **three-year cumulative historical loss position** as of the third quarter of 2024, largely resulting from the asset impairment and restructuring and other charges incurred during 2024" [INTC-10K-FY2024#p482].

Additional detail on restructuring-related impairments: $442 million of non-cash impairments of construction-in-progress assets from the decision to **exit and outsource manufacturing of certain internal test hardware**, and $103 million of impairments of operating leased assets/leasehold improvements from real estate consolidations and exits [INTC-10K-FY2024#p170].

**Note on revenue:** the loss was not primarily a revenue story — revenue fell only 2.1% to $53.101B [INTC-10K-FY2024]. The swing from +$1.689B net income in FY2023 to -$18.756B in FY2024 is driven by the ~$19.1B of combined charges above (restructuring $2.8B + manufacturing impairments/accelerated depreciation $3.3B + goodwill/intangibles $3.1B + tax valuation allowance $9.9B), with the tax charge alone accounting for roughly half the net loss.

2. **Hopper GPU platform shipments** — Compute & Networking revenue growth "was due to higher Data Center revenue. Compute grew 266% due to higher shipments of the NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform for the training and inference of LLMs, recommendation engines and generative AI applications" [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p282].
3. **Networking (InfiniBand)** — Networking up 133% "due to higher shipments of InfiniBand" [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p282]; networking is described as integral to data-center-scale computing [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p31].
4. **Inference and cloud demand** — NVIDIA estimates ~40% of FY2024 Data Center revenue was for AI inference; in Q4 FY2024 large cloud providers represented more than half of Data Center revenue [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p264]. New platforms launched: AI inference platforms combining Ada/Hopper/Grace Hopper, DGX Cloud, AI Foundations, Spectrum-X networking [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p264].
5. **Gaming** — up 15% "driven by higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels" plus growing demand; product launches GeForce RTX 4060/4070, RTX 40-Series SUPER, DLSS 3.5 [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p282; #p265].

answer:
**NVIDIA's FY2024 revenue growth was driven overwhelmingly by Data Center.**

**The numbers:** Revenue rose 125.9% to $60.9B in FY2024 (period 2023-01-30 to 2024-01-28), up from $27.0B in FY2023 [NVDA-10K-FY2024]. Gross margin expanded from 56.9% to 72.7% and operating margin from 15.7% to 54.1% [NVDA-10K-FY2024].

**What the 10-K says drove it:**
- **Data Center revenue grew 217%**, the primary driver of both the top line and the gross margin expansion [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p286].
- Within the Compute & Networking segment, **Compute grew 266%** on higher shipments of the **NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform** for training and inference of LLMs, recommendation engines and generative AI applications; **Networking rose 133%** on higher InfiniBand shipments [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p282].
- Gross margin improvement was attributed to Data Center revenue growth plus **lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue** — the net effect was a 2.7% unfavorable impact in FY2024 versus 7.5% in FY2023 [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p286].

**Other segments (much smaller contributors):** Gaming +15% on higher sell-in after channel inventory normalized, Professional Visualization +1%, Automotive +21% on self-driving platforms [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p263].

**One caveat on operating expenses:** they increased on headcount and compensation, but FY2023 had included a $1.4B acquisition termination charge related to the proposed Arm transaction, which flattered the FY2024 operating income comparison [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p263].

**Micron's FY2023 loss (year ended 2023-08-31) was driven by a severe industry downturn in memory pricing.**

**The numbers** [MU-10K-FY2023]:
- Revenue fell 49.5% to $15.54B (from $30.76B in FY2022) [MU-10K-FY2023]
- Gross margin swung from +45.2% to **−9.1%**, i.e. gross profit of −$1.42B [MU-10K-FY2023]
- Operating margin −37.0% (operating loss $5.75B); net loss $5.83B, net margin −37.5% [MU-10K-FY2023]

**The 10-K's explanation** [MU-10K-FY2023#p231]:
1. **Declines in average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND** — the primary driver of the gross margin collapse from 45% to negative 9%.
2. **Charges to write inventories down to net realizable value (NRV)**, caused by those falling ASPs. Because write-downs are recorded before the inventory is sold, they hit cost of goods sold in the period [MU-10K-FY2023#p232].
3. **$382 million of facility underutilization costs** in 2023, as Micron cut wafer starts significantly below peak capacity to burn off elevated inventory [MU-10K-FY2023#p231].

The filing frames this as an industry-wide condition: a "challenging pricing environment, elevated levels of inventories for suppliers and customers, and significant supply-demand mismatch," which led Micron to reduce capital expenditures and wafer starts [MU-10K-FY2023#p222]. Notably, there were no NRV write-downs in Q4 2023 as pricing began to improve [MU-10K-FY2023#p222].

So the loss was not a demand collapse specific to Micron or an impairment of goodwill — it was a memory price downcycle compressing gross margin below zero, amplified by inventory write-downs and underutilization charges.

Micron reported a FY2023 net loss of $5.833B (vs. $8.687B net income in FY2022) primarily because of an industry downturn that drove sharp price declines and inventory write-downs [MU-10K-FY2023; MU-10K-FY2022].

Management's stated reasons in the 10-K:

1. **Industry downturn / weak demand:** The memory and storage industry "deteriorated sharply in the fourth quarter of 2022 and throughout 2023 due to weak demand in many end markets combined with global and macroeconomic challenges and lower demand resulting from customer actions to reduce inventory levels" [MU-10K-FY2023#p221].
2. **Pricing declines:** This led to "significant reductions in average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND," cutting revenue across all segments and nearly all end markets [MU-10K-FY2023#p221]. Revenue fell 49.5% to $15.540B; DRAM sales −51% (high-40s % ASP decline) and NAND sales −46% (low-50s % ASP decline) [MU-10K-FY2023#p230].
3. **Inventory NRV write-downs:** $1.83B of charges in 2023 to write inventories down to net realizable value [MU-10K-FY2023#p221]. Gross margin fell to −9.1% from 45.2%, "primarily due to declines in average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND and charges to write down inventories" [MU-10K-FY2023#p231].
4. **Underutilization costs:** $382 million of facility underutilization costs in FY2023, with wafer starts significantly reduced for DRAM and NAND [MU-10K-FY2023#p231; MU-10K-FY2023#p222].
5. **Restructuring:** 2023 Restructure Plan with headcount reduction approaching 15% by end of calendar 2023; $171 million of restructure charges, primarily employee severance [MU-10K-FY2023#p384; MU-10K-FY2023#p226].
6. **China CAC decision:** A low-double-digit percentage of worldwide revenue (about half of China-headquartered customer revenue) "is at risk of being impacted" [MU-10K-FY2023#p226].

Operating loss was $5.745B (−37.0% of revenue) vs. $9.702B operating income in FY2022 [MU-10K-FY2023; MU-10K-FY2022].

| Operating income | $9.702B (31.5%) | −$5.745B (−37.0%) | — |
| Net income | $8.687B (28.2%) | −$5.833B (−37.5%) | — |
| R&D | $3.116B (10.1%) | $3.114B (20.0%) | flat in $ |

**Management's stated reasons (10-K, "Industry Conditions" and "Consolidated Results"):**

1. **Industry downturn / demand weakness:** "The memory and storage industry environment deteriorated sharply in the fourth quarter of 2022 and throughout 2023 due to weak demand in many end markets combined with global and macroeconomic challenges and lower demand resulting from customer actions to reduce inventory levels" [MU-10K-FY2023#p221].
2. **Pricing declines:** This "led to significant reductions in average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND and bit shipments for DRAM, resulting in declines in revenue across all our business segments and nearly all our end markets" [MU-10K-FY2023#p221]. Revenue fell 49%: DRAM sales −51% (high-40s % ASP decline, high-single-digit bit shipment decline); NAND sales −46% (low-50s % ASP decline, high-single-digit bit shipment increase) [MU-10K-FY2023#p230]. By business unit: CNBU −58%, MBU −50%, SBU −44%, EBU −31% [MU-10K-FY2023#p235].
3. **Inventory NRV write-downs:** "we recognized charges of $1.83 billion in 2023 to write down inventories to their estimated net realizable value" [MU-10K-FY2023#p221]. Gross margin fell to −9% from 45% "primarily due to declines in average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND and charges to write down inventories ... and $382 million of facility underutilization costs in 2023" [MU-10K-FY2023#p231].
4. **Underutilization costs:** $382 million of facility underutilization costs in FY2023 [MU-10K-FY2023#p231]; wafer starts significantly reduced for both DRAM and NAND [MU-10K-FY2023#p222].
5. **Restructuring:** 2023 Restructure Plan — headcount reduction approaching 15% by end of calendar 2023; restructure charges of $171 million in 2023, primarily employee severance; expected cost savings of ~$130 million per quarter [MU-10K-FY2023#p384; MU-10K-FY2023#p226].
6. **China CAC decision (additional demand headwind):** ~half of China-headquartered customer revenue, "a low-double-digit percentage of our worldwide revenue, is at risk of being impacted" [MU-10K-FY2023#p226].

**Note on the write-down figure:** the $1.83B is the gross charge recognized in FY2023; the 10-K notes the gross-margin impact is net of lower costs in the period on sales of inventory written down in prior periods [MU-10K-FY2023#p232]. Also, no NRV write-downs were recorded in Q4 2023 as pricing trends began to improve [MU-10K-FY2023#p222].

findings.answer:
## Findings: Home Depot (HD) — no net loss in any recent fiscal year

**The premise is false. HD reported a net profit, not a loss, in FY2025.**

### Fiscal-year convention note
The subtask's stated period ("FY2025 ending 02-01-2026") corresponds to the tool's **fiscal_year 2026** (period 2025-02-03..2026-02-01) [HD-10K-FY2026]. The tool's **fiscal_year 2025** is the period 2024-01-29..2025-02-02 [HD-10K-FY2025]. I report both.

### Reported figures (USD billions)

| Metric | FY2024 (ended 2024-01-28) | FY2025 (ended 2025-02-02) | FY2026 (ended 2026-02-01) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 152.669 | 159.514 | 164.683 |
| Gross profit | 50.960 | 53.308 | 54.865 |
| Operating income | 21.689 | 21.526 | 20.890 |
| **Net income** | **15.143** | **14.806** | **14.156** |
| Gross margin | 33.4% | 33.4% | 33.3% |
| Operating margin | 14.2% | 13.5% | 12.7% |
| Net margin | 9.9% | 9.3% | 8.6% |
| Revenue growth | −3.0% | +4.5% | +3.2% |

Sources: [HD-10K-FY2024], [HD-10K-FY2025], [HD-10K-FY2026].

Net income was positive in every year: $15.1B → $14.8B → $14.2B. The change is a **modest decline in profitability** (net margin 9.9% → 9.3% → 8.6%), not a loss.

### No unusual or one-time charges found
- Goodwill: "no events or circumstances that would indicate that it is more likely than not that the fair value of any of these reporting units was less than its carrying amount. There were also no impairment charges related to goodwill in fiscal 2023 or fiscal 2022" [HD-10K-FY2025#p316].
- Intangibles: "no impairment losses should be recognized. There were no impairment charges related to any of our definite or indefinite-lived intangible assets in fiscal 2024, fiscal 2023, or fiscal 2022" [HD-10K-FY2025#p318]; and for FY2025: "no impairment charges related to any of our definite or indefinite-lived intangible assets in fiscal 2025, fiscal 2024, or fiscal 2023" [HD-10K-FY2026#p324].
- Long-lived assets: "Impairment charges for long-lived assets were not material... in fiscal 2024, fiscal 2023, or fiscal 2022" [HD-10K-FY2025#p265].
- No restructuring or settlement charge was identified; litigation appears only as a risk factor [HD-10K-FY2025#p165].

### Actual drivers of the profitability decline (quoted)
**FY2025 (period ending 2025-02-02):**
- Gross profit: "Gross profit increased $2.3 billion, or 4.6%, to $53.3 billion in fiscal 2024. Gross profit as a percent of net sales... was 33.4% for both fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023, and primarily reflected lower transportation costs and lower shrink within our Primary segment, offset by the inclusion of SRS in our consolidated results" [HD-10K-FY2025#p201].
- SG&A: "SG&A increased $2.2 billion, or 8.1%, to $28.7 billion in fiscal 2024. As a percent of net sales, SG&A was 18.0%... compared to 17.4%..., which primarily reflects higher payroll costs, deleverage from a negative comparable sales environment and lower legal-related benefits" [HD-10K-FY2025#p202].
- D&A: "increased $361 million, or 13.5%, to $3.0 billion... primarily reflecting increased intangible asset amortization expense of $239 million, of which $218 million was related to SRS" [HD-10K-FY2025#p202].
- Note: fiscal 2024 included 53 weeks [HD-10K-FY2025#p208].

**FY2026 (period ending 2026-02-01):**
- Gross profit: "Gross profit increased $1.6 billion, or 2.9%, to $54.9 billion in fiscal 2025. Gross profit... margin was 33.3% in fiscal 2025 compared to 33.4% in fiscal 2024. The decrease in gross profit margin reflects the inclusion of SRS and GMS in our consolidated results, partially offset by lower shrink and certain supply chain benefits within our Primary segment" [HD-10K-FY2026#p211].
- SG&A: "SG&A increased $2.0 billion, or 6.8%, to $30.7 billion in fiscal 2025. As a percent of net sales, SG&A was 18.6% in fiscal 2025 compared to 18.0% in fiscal 2024, which primarily reflects higher payroll and related costs in fiscal 2025 along with the impact of a non-recurring legal-related benefit recognized during fiscal 2024 within our Primary segment" [HD-10K-FY2026#p212].
- D&A: "increased $239 million, or 7.9%, to $3.3 billion... primarily reflects increased intangible asset amortization expense resulting from our acquisitions of SRS and GMS" [HD-10K-FY2026#p212].
- EPS: "Diluted earnings per share were $14.23 in fiscal 2025 compared to $14.91 in fiscal 2024. The decrease... was primarily driven by lower net earnings" [HD-10K-FY2026#p215].

**Summary:** HD's profitability decline is driven by SG&A deleverage (higher payroll, acquisition mix from SRS/GMS, and lapping a non-recurring FY2024 legal-related benefit) plus higher D&A from acquisition-related intangible amortization — not by any impairment, write-down, restructuring, or settlement charge.

Among the five software companies examined, **ServiceNow (NOW)** had the lowest FY2024 operating margin at **12.4%** (operating income $1.364B on revenue $10.984B) [NOW-10K-FY2024]. Per its FY2024 10-K, the main drivers of the increase in ServiceNow's operating expenses were:
- **Sales and marketing** rose **$553M**, mainly from increased headcount → personnel-related costs including stock-based compensation and overhead of **$330M**; amortization of deferred commissions **+$90M**; other program expenses (branding, advertising, marketing events, market data) **+$95M** [NOW-10K-FY2024#p271, #p272].
- **R&D** rose **$419M**, primarily increased headcount → personnel-related costs including SBC and overhead of **$350M**; outside services **+$48M**; software/maintenance and data-center capacity **+$27M**; partly offset by **−$12M** lower program spend [NOW-10K-FY2024#p273].

Note: the question's premise that operating expenses increased does not hold for Salesforce — its FY2024 operating expenses *decreased* across all three categories (S&M headcount −14%, G&A headcount −20%), which the 10-K attributes to its Restructuring Plan and hiring pause [CRM-10K-FY2024#p328, #p329, #p330].

findings.task: For MSFT (Microsoft Corp), fiscal year 2024 (fiscal year ends 06-30), find operating income and total revenue to compute the operating margin. Also search the FY2024 10-K for the main drivers of the increase in operating expenses.
findings.answer:
## MSFT — Fiscal Year 2024 (period 2023-07-01 to 2024-06-30)

**Operating margin: 44.6%** [MSFT-10K-FY2024]

| Metric | FY2024 |
|---|---|
| Total revenue | $245.122B [MSFT-10K-FY2024] |
| Operating income | $109.433B [MSFT-10K-FY2024] |
| Operating margin | 44.6% [MSFT-10K-FY2024] |
| Gross margin | 69.8% [MSFT-10K-FY2024] |
| R&D as % of revenue | 12.0% [MSFT-10K-FY2024] |
| Revenue growth | 15.7% [MSFT-10K-FY2024] |

**Drivers of the increase in operating expenses** (per FY2024 10-K):

- **R&D:** increased **$2.3B, or 9%**, driven by Gaming — with **7 points of growth from the Activision Blizzard acquisition** — and investments in cloud engineering [MSFT-10K-FY2024#p268].
- **Sales and marketing:** increased **$1.7B, or 7%**, driven by Gaming, with **6 points of growth from the Activision Blizzard acquisition** [MSFT-10K-FY2024#p269].
- **General and administrative:** increased only slightly, as growth from the Activision Blizzard acquisition was offset in part by a prior-year Q2 charge [MSFT-10K-FY2024#p270].
- **Segment context (More Personal Computing):** operating expenses increased **$3.9B, or 31%**, driven by Gaming, with 34 points of net impact from the Activision Blizzard acquisition [MSFT-10K-FY2024#p266]. The $75.4B Activision Blizzard acquisition closed October 13, 2023 and its results are consolidated from that date [MSFT-10K-FY2024#p233].

**Note for the final answer:** MSFT's 44.6% operating margin is high, not low — it is unlikely to be the lowest-margin software company in FY2024.

findings.task: For CRM (Salesforce, Inc.), fiscal year 2024 (fiscal year ends 01-31), find operating income and total revenue to compute the operating margin. Also search the FY2024 10-K for the main drivers of the increase in operating expenses.
findings.answer:
## Findings: Salesforce, Inc. (CRM), FY2024 (period 2023-02-01 to 2024-01-31)

**Operating margin — FY2024**
- Total revenue: **$34.857B** [CRM-10K-FY2024]
- Operating income: **$5.011B** [CRM-10K-FY2024]
- **Operating margin: 14.4%** (server-computed) [CRM-10K-FY2024]
- Context: gross margin 75.5%, net margin 11.9%, revenue growth 11.2% [CRM-10K-FY2024]
- 10-K confirms: revenue $34.9B, up 11% YoY; income from operations $5.0B vs $1.0B a year ago; operating margin ~14% vs ~3% in the prior year [CRM-10K-FY2024#p285]

**Important correction to the question's premise:** Salesforce's FY2024 operating expenses did **not** increase — they *decreased* in absolute dollars and as a percentage of revenue across all three categories. The 10-K attributes the margin expansion to lower operating expenses, not higher ones.

**Drivers of the operating expense *decrease* (per the FY2024 10-K):**
- **Sales and marketing:** decrease primarily due to lower employee-related costs, including stock-based compensation; marketing and sales headcount **fell 14%** during FY2024, driven by restructuring initiatives and a hiring pause in effect during the year [CRM-10K-FY2024#p329]
- **General and administrative:** decrease primarily due to lower employee-related costs, including stock-based compensation; G&A headcount **fell 20%** during FY2024, driven by the Restructuring Plan and the hiring pause [CRM-10K-FY2024#p330]
- **Research and development:** decrease primarily due to lower employee-related costs, including stock-based compensation; however, at the end of FY2024 the company began investing in incremental AI resources, and R&D headcount **rose 5%** during FY2024 [CRM-10K-FY2024#p328]
- **Restructuring Plan:** ~**$988M** of costs incurred in FY2024, of which ~**$541M** was employee transition/severance/benefits/stock-based comp and ~**$447M** was exit charges from office space reductions [CRM-10K-FY2024#p330]. The plan included a ~10% workforce reduction and office space reductions, substantially complete as of Q1 FY2024, plus an additional focused workforce reduction initiated and substantially completed in Q4 FY2024 [CRM-10K-FY2024#p284]
- Management noted it has "started to see improvements in our operating expenses across all operating categories, with the most opportunity in sales and marketing expense and general and administrative expenses" [CRM-10K-FY2024#p284]

**Bottom line for the team:** CRM's FY2024 operating margin was **14.4%** — a high margin, so CRM is very unlikely to be the lowest-operating-margin software company in FY2024.

findings.task: For ADBE (Adobe Inc.), fiscal year 2024 (fiscal year ends 11-28), find operating income and total revenue to compute the operating margin. Also search the FY2024 10-K for the main drivers of the increase in operating expenses.
findings.answer:
**ADBE — FY2024 (period 2023-12-02 to 2024-11-29) [ADBE-10K-FY2024]**

- Revenue: $21.505B; Operating income: $6.741B; **Operating margin: 31.3%** (server-computed) [ADBE-10K-FY2024]
- Gross margin 89.0%; R&D as % of revenue 18.3%; revenue growth 10.8% [ADBE-10K-FY2024]

**Drivers of operating expense increases (FY2024 10-K):**
- **R&D**: expense consists mainly of compensation and contracted software-development costs, third-party hosting services and data center costs **including AI training costs**; R&D increased on these items [ADBE-10K-FY2024#p283].
- **Sales and marketing**: compensation costs, amortization of contract acquisition costs (sales commissions), travel/facilities, plus revenue-generating programs (advertising, trade shows, PR); S&M increased on these [ADBE-10K-FY2024#p285].
- **G&A**: compensation/contracted costs, travel, facilities for finance/HR/legal/IS/executive, outside legal and accounting fees; G&A increased, and FY2024 included **costs from optimization of leased facilities — impairment charges on certain operating lease right-of-use assets and leasehold improvements** [ADBE-10K-FY2024#p286, #p287].
- **Cost of subscription revenue** includes third-party hosting/data center costs and **AI inferencing costs**; cost of subscription revenue decreased [ADBE-10K-FY2024#p279]. Cost of services and other revenue rose on higher compensation costs and professional fees [ADBE-10K-FY2024#p282].

Note: the 10-K passages give the composition and direction of each expense line but the specific dollar/percentage breakdown tables were not returned by the search.

findings.task: For NOW (ServiceNow, Inc.), fiscal year 2024 (fiscal year ends 12-31), find operating income and total revenue to compute the operating margin. Also search the FY2024 10-K for the main drivers of the increase in operating expenses.
findings.answer:
**ServiceNow (NOW), FY2024 (period 2024-01-01..2024-12-31, 10-K filed 2025-01-30) [NOW-10K-FY2024]**

- Total revenue: **$10.984B** (revenue growth +22.4%) [NOW-10K-FY2024]
- Operating income: **$1.364B** [NOW-10K-FY2024]
- Operating margin: **12.4%** (server-computed) [NOW-10K-FY2024]
- (Context: gross profit $8.697B, net income $1.425B, R&D = 23.2% of revenue) [NOW-10K-FY2024]

**Drivers of the increase in operating expenses (FY2024 10-K, "Cost of Revenues and Gross Profit Percentage" / expense discussion):**
- **Sales and marketing** rose **$553M**, mainly from increased headcount → personnel-related costs including stock-based compensation and overhead of **$330M**; amortization of deferred commissions **+$90M** (more new-customer, expansion and renewal contracts); other program expenses (branding, advertising, marketing events, market data) **+$95M**, partly for the annual Sales Kickoff and Knowledge user conference [NOW-10K-FY2024#p271, #p272]
- **R&D** rose **$419M**, primarily increased headcount → personnel-related costs including SBC and overhead of **$350M**; outside services **+$48M**; software/maintenance and other costs to expand data center capacity **+$27M**; partly offset by **-$12M** lower program spend [NOW-10K-FY2024#p273]
- Cost of revenues: professional services gross loss improved due to revenue growth and lower fixed personnel-related costs (incl. SBC) as the company shifts a portion of professional services to variable spending with strategic third-party partners [NOW-10K-FY2024#p271]

Note: NOW's 12.4% operating margin is relatively high for the group; it is unlikely to be the lowest-margin software company in FY2024.

findings.task: For CSCO (Cisco Systems, Inc.), fiscal year 2024 (fiscal year ends 07-25), find operating income and total revenue to compute the operating margin. Also search the FY2024 10-K for the main drivers of the increase in operating expenses.
findings.answer:
**CSCO — FY2024 (period 2023-07-30 to 2024-07-27) [CSCO-10K-FY2024]**

- Revenue: $53.803B; operating income: $12.181B; **operating margin: 22.6%** (server-computed) [CSCO-10K-FY2024]. Gross margin 64.7%, R&D 14.8% of revenue, revenue growth −5.6% [CSCO-10K-FY2024].

**Drivers of higher operating expenses (FY2024 10-K):**
- Overall: operating income fell 19% and operating margin fell 3.8 pp, driven by lower revenue, incremental operating expenses from Splunk, higher restructuring and other charges, and higher amortization of purchased intangible assets, partly offset by higher gross margin percentage [CSCO-10K-FY2024#p282]. In the Q4 snapshot, R&D + sales & marketing + G&A collectively rose 8.1 pp as a % of revenue, and operating margin fell 8.8 pp in the quarter, primarily on incremental Splunk operating expenses and higher amortization of purchased intangibles [CSCO-10K-FY2024#p226].
- R&D: higher share-based compensation, incremental Splunk expenses, higher cash compensation from acquisitions, higher discretionary spending; partly offset by lower headcount-related and variable compensation [CSCO-10K-FY2024#p275].
- Sales & marketing: incremental Splunk expenses, higher share-based compensation, higher discretionary spending, higher headcount-related expenses and higher cash compensation from acquisitions; partly offset by lower contracted services and variable compensation [CSCO-10K-FY2024#p276].
- G&A: higher acquisition-related costs, incremental Splunk expenses, higher share-based compensation, higher discretionary spending and headcount-related expenses; partly offset by lower contracted services and variable compensation [CSCO-10K-FY2024#p277].
- Amortization of purchased intangibles rose, including $569M from Splunk, plus $145M of impairment charges on IPR&D intangibles [CSCO-10K-FY2024#p279].

answer:
**ServiceNow (NOW)** had the lowest operating margin among the software companies in fiscal year 2024.

FY2024 operating margins (fiscal year ending in calendar 2024):
- ServiceNow: **12.4%** (operating income $1.364B on revenue $10.984B) [NOW-10K-FY2024]
- Salesforce: 14.4% ($5.011B / $34.857B) [CRM-10K-FY2024]
- Cisco: 22.6% ($12.181B / $53.803B) [CSCO-10K-FY2024]
- Adobe: 31.3% ($6.741B / $21.505B) [ADBE-10K-FY2024]
- Microsoft: 44.6% ($109.433B / $245.122B) [MSFT-10K-FY2024]

**Drivers of the increase in ServiceNow's operating expenses (per its FY2024 10-K):**

- **Sales and marketing: +$553M** — mainly increased headcount, driving higher personnel-related costs including stock-based compensation and overhead of $330M; amortization of deferred commissions rose $90M on more new-customer, expansion and renewal contracts; other program expenses (branding, advertising, marketing events, market data) rose $95M, largely from the annual Sales Kickoff and Knowledge user conference [NOW-10K-FY2024#p271, #p272]
- **Research and development: +$419M** — increased headcount driving personnel-related costs including stock-based compensation and overhead of $350M; outside services +$48M; software, maintenance and other costs to support data center capacity expansion +$27M; partly offset by a $12M decrease in program spend [NOW-10K-FY2024#p273]
- **General and administrative: +$73M** — higher headcount raising personnel costs excluding stock-based compensation by $37M, plus $67M in other corporate expenses and outside services, partly offset by a $36M decrease in stock-based compensation as the requisite service period of certain performance awards was met [NOW-10K-FY2024#p275]

In short, the increases were overwhelmingly headcount-driven personnel costs (including stock-based compensation), supplemented by commission amortization, marketing events, outside services and data center capacity costs [NOW-10K-FY2024#p263].

answer:
**Lowe's (fiscal year ended 2025-01-31):**
- Comparable sales **decreased 2.7%**, driven by a 3.0% decline in comparable customer transactions and a 0.3% increase in comparable average ticket [LOW-10K-FY2025#p166].
- Total revenue fell **3.1%** to $83.674B [LOW-10K-FY2025], so the total revenue decline was slightly steeper than the comparable sales decline — the filing attributes the total sales decrease primarily to the comparable sales decrease [LOW-10K-FY2025#p166].

**Best Buy (fiscal year ended 2025-02-01):**
- Total revenue fell **4.4%** to $41.528B [BBY-10K-FY2025].
- The filing explains the Domestic segment revenue decline as driven primarily by comparable sales declines in appliances and home theater, plus the extra week of revenue (~$675M) in the prior year [BBY-10K-FY2025#p181]. Category-level comparable changes included Appliances −14.8%, Entertainment −11.9%, Consumer Electronics −5.2%, offset by Computing & Mobile Phones +3.4% and Services +8.4% [BBY-10K-FY2025#p182]. Online revenue of $13.0B decreased 0.8% on a comparable basis [BBY-10K-FY2025#p181].
- **Caveat:** the specific enterprise-wide comparable sales percentage for Best Buy is not stated in the passages retrieved, so I can't give that figure — only the category-level comparable changes and the total revenue change.

**Comparison:** Both retailers saw total revenue decline in the year ending early 2025 (Lowe's −3.1%, Best Buy −4.4%), with comparable sales declines as the primary driver in both cases. Lowe's quantified its comparable decline at 2.7%, slightly less negative than its total revenue change; Best Buy's total revenue decline was amplified by the prior year's extra week (~$675M) [BBY-10K-FY2025#p181].

**Lowe's (fiscal year ended January 31, 2025):** Comparable sales fell **−2.7%** [LOW-10K-FY2025#p166], while total revenue fell **−3.1%**, from $86.377 billion to $83.674 billion [LOW-10K-FY2025][LOW-10K-FY2024]. So the revenue decline slightly exceeded the comparable sales decline, with no material store-count/calendar effect (both years had 52 weeks) [LOW-10K-FY2025#p158].

**Best Buy:** No result — the researcher stopped without returning data (max_steps), so Best Buy's comparable sales change, total revenue for the year and prior year, and revenue change are missing and cannot be reported.

findings.answer:
## Findings: The premise is false — Home Depot did NOT report a net loss

**Correction:** HD reported **positive net income** in every year available. There was no net loss in FY2025 (or FY2026).

### Income statement metrics (USD billions)

| Metric | FY2024 (ended 2024-01-28) | FY2025 (ended 2025-02-02) | FY2026 (ended 2026-02-01) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 152.669 | 159.514 | 164.683 |
| Gross profit | 50.960 | 53.308 | 54.865 |
| Operating income | 21.689 | 21.526 | 20.890 |
| **Net income** | **15.143** | **14.806** | **14.156** |
| Gross margin | 33.4% | 33.4% | 33.3% |
| Operating margin | 14.2% | 13.5% | 12.7% |
| Net margin | 9.9% | 9.3% | 8.6% |
| Revenue growth | −3.0% | +4.5% | +3.2% |

Sources: [HD-10K-FY2024], [HD-10K-FY2025], [HD-10K-FY2026]

**Note on fiscal-year convention:** the subtask's "FY2025 ending 02-01-2026" is, under this server's convention, **fiscal_year 2026** (period 2025-02-03..2026-02-01) [HD-10K-FY2026]. The server's fiscal_year 2025 is the year ended 2025-02-02 [HD-10K-FY2025]. Both years show profits; the FY2025 10-K (filed 2025-03-21) is the filing that explains the FY2025 earnings decline.

### Stated reasons for the earnings decline (FY2025 10-K, year ended 2025-02-02)

Net income fell from $15.143B to $14.806B (−$0.34B, −2.2%) even as revenue rose 4.5% [HD-10K-FY2025]. Drivers per the filing:

1. **SG&A growth outpacing sales** — "SG&A increased $2.2 billion, or 8.1%, to $28.7 billion in fiscal 2024. As a percent of net sales, SG&A was 18.0% in fiscal 2024 compared to 17.4% in fiscal 2023, which primarily reflects higher payroll costs, deleverage from a negative comparable sales environment and lower legal-related benefits." [HD-10K-FY2025#p202]
2. **Higher D&A, largely SRS acquisition-related intangible amortization** — "Depreciation and amortization increased $361 million, or 13.5%, to $3.0 billion... primarily reflecting increased intangible asset amortization expense of $239 million, of which $218 million was related to SRS, as well as increased depreciation expense from ongoing investments in the business." [HD-10K-FY2025#p202] Total intangible amortization was $425M in fiscal 2024 vs $186M in fiscal 2023 [HD-10K-FY2025#p317].
3. **Higher interest expense from more long-term debt** — "Interest and other, net increased $355 million, or 20.1%, to $2.1 billion in fiscal 2024... primarily due to higher interest expense driven by higher long-term debt." [HD-10K-FY2025#p203]
4. **Partially offsetting: gross margin held flat** — "Gross profit increased $2.3 billion, or 4.6%, to $53.3 billion... gross profit margin was 33.4% for both fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023, and primarily reflected lower transportation costs and lower shrink within our Primary segment, offset by the inclusion of SRS in our consolidated results." [HD-10K-FY2025#p201]
5. **Tax rate slightly favorable** — effective tax rate 23.7% in fiscal 2024 vs 24.0% in fiscal 2023 [HD-10K-FY2025#p204]. Diluted EPS $14.91 vs $15.11, with the 53rd week adding ~$0.30 [HD-10K-FY2025#p205].

**No goodwill write-down, impairment charge, or litigation charge was identified** in the FY2025 10-K as a cause of a loss — the decline was margin/expense-driven (payroll, SRS amortization, interest), not a one-time charge.

For the fiscal year ended 2025-02-02 (fiscal_year 2025):
- Revenue: $159.514B, up 4.5% year over year [HD-10K-FY2025]
- Gross profit: $53.308B [HD-10K-FY2025]
- Operating income: $21.526B [HD-10K-FY2025]
- Net income: $14.806B, a net margin of 9.3% [HD-10K-FY2025]

So the company was solidly profitable. What likely prompted the question is that net income *declined* modestly versus FY2024 ($15.143B, 9.9% net margin) [HD-10K-FY2024], even as revenue grew 4.5% — i.e., margin compression, not a loss. **Lowest net margin, FY2024:**
1. **INTC** — −35.3% (a net loss) [INTC-10K-FY2024]

answer:
**NVIDIA:** FY2024 revenue growth was **+125.9%** ($60.922B vs $26.974B) [NVDA-10K-FY2024]. Main reason per the 10-K: Data Center revenue **up 217%**, driven by higher shipments of the Hopper GPU platform for LLM training/inference, recommendation engines and generative AI, plus InfiniBand networking growth [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p262][NVDA-10K-FY2024#p282].

**AMD:** FY2024 revenue growth was **+13.7%** ($25.785B vs $22.68B); the 10-K states "increasing 14%" [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282]. Main reasons: growth "driven by the performance of our Data Center and Client segments" — Data Center **+94%** on higher AMD Instinct GPU and EPYC CPU sales, Client **+52%** on higher Ryzen mobile/desktop processor sales, partly offset by Gaming **−58%** (lower semi-custom revenue) and lower Embedded [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282].

**Intel:** FY2024 revenue growth was **−2.1%** ($53.101B vs $54.228B); the 10-K states revenue "down $1.1 billion, or 2%" [INTC-10K-FY2024#p157]. Main reasons: lower "all other" revenue (−32%, including lower Altera and Mobileye revenue as customers reduced inventories) and lower Intel Foundry external revenue (−60%), partially offset by higher Intel Products revenue (+3%) [INTC-10K-FY2024#p157][INTC-10K-FY2024#p130].

**Main reason for the change, per the FY2024 10-K**

- Demand was "driven by enterprise software and consumer internet applications, and multiple industry verticals including automotive, financial services, and healthcare," with customers accessing NVIDIA AI infrastructure both via cloud and on-premises [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p262].
- Compute & Networking growth was "due to higher Data Center revenue… higher shipments of the NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform for the training and inference of LLMs, recommendation engines and generative AI applications"; networking up 133% on higher InfiniBand shipments [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p282].
- Other segments: Gaming +15% (higher sell-in after channel inventory normalization), ProViz +1%, Automotive +21% (self-driving platforms) [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p262, #p263].

**AMD (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.) — FY2023 vs FY2024**

**Main reasons for the change (per the FY2024 10-K)**
- Growth "was driven by the performance of our Data Center and Client segments" [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282].
- **Data Center:** net revenue of $12.6B, **+94%** vs $6.5B in 2023, "primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct™ GPUs and AMD EPYC™ CPUs"; segment operating income rose to $3.5B from $1.3B on higher revenue, partly offset by higher R&D [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282][AMD-10K-FY2024#p307].

- **Partially offsetting declines:** **Gaming** net revenue $2.6B, **−58%** vs $6.2B, "primarily due to lower semi-custom product revenue"; **Embedded** also declined (net revenue $3.6B) [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282].

## Intel (INTC) — FY2024 revenue and drivers

**Revenue**
- FY2023: **$54.228B** (period 2023-01-01..2023-12-30) [INTC-10K-FY2023]
- FY2024: **$53.101B** (period 2023-12-31..2024-12-28) [INTC-10K-FY2024]
- FY2024 revenue growth: **−2.1%** (server-computed) [INTC-10K-FY2024]; the 10-K states revenue "down $1.1 billion, or 2%, from 2023" [INTC-10K-FY2024#p157]

**Main reasons for the decline (per the 10-K)**
The company attributes the $1.1B / 2% decrease to **lower "all other" revenue and lower Intel Foundry revenue, partially offset by higher Intel Products revenue** [INTC-10K-FY2024#p157][INTC-10K-FY2024#p98]:
- **All other revenue −32%** ($3.8B, down $1.8B): lower **Altera** revenue ($1.5B, down $1.3B) as customers tempered purchases to reduce existing inventories across all product lines, and lower **Mobileye** revenue ($1.7B, down $425M) as customers reduced inventories of EyeQ products [INTC-10K-FY2024#p157][INTC-10K-FY2024#p154]
- **Intel Foundry external revenue −60%**: lower traditional packaging services and lower equipment sales [INTC-10K-FY2024#p157]
- **Offset — Intel Products revenue +3%** to $48.9B (up $1.3B) [INTC-10K-FY2024#p130]:
  - **CCG +$1.0B (+4%)**: notebook revenue $19.1B, up $2.1B, on **notebook volume +12%** as customer inventory levels improved vs. 2023; partly offset by desktop revenue $9.7B (−$516M, volume −5% on lower demand) and other CCG $1.6B (−$530M, exit of legacy businesses) [INTC-10K-FY2024#p130]
  - **DCAI +$182M (+1%)**: higher server revenue; server ASPs +12% on higher mix of high core count products, server volume −10% on lower demand [INTC-10K-FY2024#p130][INTC-10K-FY2024#p158]

Note: FY2024 also included $7.0B of restructuring and other charges and $9.9B of deferred-tax valuation allowances, excluded from segment results [INTC-10K-FY2024#p105] — these affect profit, not revenue.

findings.answer:
## MSFT — Fiscal Year 2024 (period 2023-07-01 to 2024-06-30)

**Operating margin: 44.6%** [MSFT-10K-FY2024]
- Total revenue: **$245.122B** [MSFT-10K-FY2024]
- Operating income: **$109.433B** [MSFT-10K-FY2024]
- (Server-computed operating_margin = 44.6%; gross margin 69.8%; R&D 12.0% of revenue; revenue growth 15.7% YoY) [MSFT-10K-FY2024]

**Main drivers of the increase in operating expenses (FY2024 10-K):**
- **Research and development:** increased **$2.3B, or 9%**, driven by Gaming — with **7 points of growth from the Activision Blizzard acquisition** — plus investments in cloud engineering [MSFT-10K-FY2024#p268].
- **Sales and marketing:** increased **$1.7B, or 7%**, driven by Gaming, with **6 points of growth from the Activision Blizzard acquisition** [MSFT-10K-FY2024#p269].
- **General and administrative:** increased only slightly, as growth from the Activision Blizzard acquisition was offset in part by the prior year Q2 charge [MSFT-10K-FY2024#p270].
- Context: Activision Blizzard acquisition completed October 13, 2023 for a total purchase price of **$75.4B**, reported in the More Personal Computing segment [MSFT-10K-FY2024#p386].

**Note for the final answer:** MSFT's 44.6% operating margin is high, so MSFT is unlikely to be the lowest-margin software company in FY2024 — the other researchers' companies should be compared.

findings.task: For CRM (Salesforce, Inc.), fiscal year 2024 (fiscal year ends 01-31), find operating income and total revenue to compute the operating margin. Also search the FY2024 10-K for the main drivers of the increase in operating expenses.
findings.answer:
## Findings: Salesforce, Inc. (CRM), FY2024 (period 2023-02-01 to 2024-01-31)

**Operating margin — FY2024**
- Total revenue: **$34.857B** [CRM-10K-FY2024]
- Operating income: **$5.011B** [CRM-10K-FY2024]
- Operating margin: **14.4%** [CRM-10K-FY2024] (server-computed; gross margin 75.5%, net income $4.136B, revenue growth 11.2%, R&D 14.1% of revenue)

**Important correction to the question's premise:** Salesforce's operating expenses did **not** increase in FY2024 — they *decreased* in absolute dollars and as a percentage of revenue, and operating margin expanded sharply from 3.3% in FY2023 (operating income $1.030B on revenue $31.352B) to 14.4% in FY2024 [CRM-10K-FY2023; CRM-10K-FY2024]. So CRM is unlikely to be the lowest-operating-margin software company in FY2024, and its 10-K describes expense *decreases*, not increases.

**What the FY2024 10-K says drove the expense changes (all decreases):**
- **Restructuring Plan** — ~10% workforce reduction and office-space reductions, substantially complete in Q1 FY2024; plus an additional focused workforce reduction initiated and substantially completed in Q4 FY2024. Management said improvements were seen "across all operating categories, with the most opportunity in sales and marketing expense and general and administrative expenses" [CRM-10K-FY2024#p284].
- **Marketing and sales** — decreased in absolute dollars and as % of revenue primarily due to lower employee-related costs including stock-based compensation; marketing and sales headcount **down 14%** in FY2024 from restructuring and a hiring pause [CRM-10K-FY2024#p329].
- **General and administrative** — decreased in absolute dollars and as % of revenue primarily due to lower employee-related costs including stock-based compensation; G&A headcount **down 20%** [CRM-10K-FY2024#p330].
- **Research and development** — decreased in absolute dollars and as % of revenue primarily due to lower employee-related costs including stock-based compensation, though at the end of FY2024 the company began investing in incremental AI resources, and R&D headcount **rose 5%** [CRM-10K-FY2024#p328].
- **Restructuring charges** — ~**$988M** of costs incurred in FY2024, of which ~**$541M** employee transition/severance/benefits/stock-based comp and ~**$447M** exit charges for office-space reductions [CRM-10K-FY2024#p330].
- **Cost of revenues** — increased in absolute dollars primarily due to higher enterprise cloud computing services and data center capacity, partly offset by lower third-party expenses; as % of revenue it fell ~2 points on lower relative employee-related costs and reduced third-party expenses; cost of revenues headcount down 2% [CRM-10K-FY2024#p326].

**Note for the final answer:** if the team's comparison shows CRM with the lowest FY2024 operating margin, that conflicts with the 14.4% figure above; the lowest-margin software company is likely a different ticker.

Intel's FY2024 loss was driven mainly by large non-cash charges, not just weak operations.

**Headline numbers (FY2024, period ended 2024-12-28)** [INTC-10K-FY2024]:
- Revenue: $53.101B, down 2.1% year over year
- Gross margin: 32.7% (vs 40.0% in FY2023)
- Operating income: **–$11.678B** (operating margin –22.0%)
- Net income: **–$18.756B** (net margin –35.3%)

**Why, per the 10-K** [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103]:
1. **$2.8B of restructuring charges** under the 2024 Restructuring Plan announced in Q3 2024, aimed at cutting roughly 15% of the core Intel workforce by early 2025, plus lower opex and capex [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103][INTC-10K-FY2024#p476].
2. **$3.3B of charges** — substantially all in cost of sales — for non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation of manufacturing assets, a substantial majority tied to the Intel 7 process node [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103].
3. **$3.1B of non-cash goodwill and acquired-intangible impairments** for certain reporting units [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103][INTC-10K-FY2024#p170].
4. **$9.9B of non-cash income-tax charges**, substantially related to valuation allowances recorded against net deferred tax assets [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103] — this is the main reason the net loss (–$18.8B) is far larger than the operating loss (–$11.7B).

Additional smaller items included $442M of impairments on construction-in-progress assets from exiting/outsourcing manufacturing of certain internal test hardware, and $103M of impairments on leased assets and leasehold improvements from real estate consolidations [INTC-10K-FY2024#p170].

In short: a modest revenue decline and margin compression, compounded by restructuring, manufacturing-asset impairments/accelerated depreciation, goodwill impairments, and a large deferred-tax valuation allowance.

Intel's FY2024 10-K attributes the large net loss to a combination of charges and margin compression [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103]:

- **Revenue** fell 2.1% to $53.101B, and **gross margin** dropped from 40.0% to 32.7%, partly due to $3.3B of non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation of manufacturing assets (substantially tied to the Intel 7 node) [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103].
- **Restructuring charges of $2.8B** under the 2024 Restructuring Plan (including $2.2B severance/benefits) [INTC-10K-FY2024#p102, #p103, #p168].
- **$3.1B of non-cash goodwill and acquired-intangible impairments** ($3.0B goodwill + $108M intangibles) [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103, #p481].
- **$9.9B of non-cash income-tax charges**, substantially valuation allowances on deferred tax assets, which the 10-K ties to a three-year cumulative historical loss position [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103, #p482].
- Other items: $442M construction-in-progress impairment, $103M leased-asset impairment, and a $780M R2 litigation charge [INTC-10K-FY2024#p168, #p170].

This produced an **operating loss of $11.678B** and a **net loss of $18.756B**; the gap between them is driven mainly by the $9.9B tax valuation allowance [INTC-10K-FY2024#p104, #p482].

findings.answer:
## INTC FY2024 — Why Intel reported a large net loss

**Headline results (FY2024, period 2023-12-31..2024-12-28) [INTC-10K-FY2024]:**
- Revenue: **$53.101B**, down **2.1%** YoY (from $54.228B in FY2023)
- Gross profit: **$17.345B**; gross margin **32.7%** (vs 40.0% in FY2023)
- Operating income: **–$11.678B** (operating margin **–22.0%**; vs +$0.093B / 0.2% in FY2023)
- Net income: **–$18.756B** (net margin **–35.3%**; vs +$1.689B / 3.1% in FY2023)
- R&D: **$16.546B** (31.2% of revenue)

**Loss drivers disclosed in the 10-K** — the filing explicitly lists the material items behind the 2024 results [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103]:
1. **Restructuring charges of $2.8B** under the 2024 Restructuring Plan (announced Q3 2024), which targets an ~15% reduction in core Intel workforce by early 2025 [INTC-10K-FY2024#p102, #p103]. Within this, employee severance/benefits were **$2.2B** and other streamlining actions **$294M** [INTC-10K-FY2024#p168].
2. **$3.3B of charges, substantially all in cost of sales**, for non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation of certain manufacturing assets, a substantial majority tied to the **Intel 7 process node** [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103].
3. **$3.1B of non-cash goodwill and acquired-intangible impairment charges** for certain reporting units [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103, #p170]. Goodwill impairment alone was **$3.0B**, plus a **$108M** intangible impairment [INTC-10K-FY2024#p481].
4. **$9.9B of non-cash charges in provision for income taxes**, substantially related to **valuation allowances on net deferred tax assets** [INTC-10K-FY2024#p103, #p104]. The 10-K explains the Q3 2024 assessment concluded it was "more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be recoverable based upon our three-year cumulative historical loss position," largely resulting from the 2024 asset impairment and restructuring charges [INTC-10K-FY2024#p482].
5. Additional items: **$442M** non-cash impairment of construction-in-progress (exit/outsource of internal test hardware manufacturing), **$103M** impairment of operating leased assets/leasehold improvements from real estate consolidations, and a **$780M** litigation charge from the R2 litigation [INTC-10K-FY2024#p170, #p168].

**NVIDIA's FY2024 revenue growth was driven overwhelmingly by Data Center.**

**The numbers:** Revenue rose from $26.97B in FY2023 to $60.92B in FY2024, a **+125.9%** increase [NVDA-10K-FY2024]. Gross margin expanded from 56.9% to 72.7% and operating margin from 15.7% to 54.1% [NVDA-10K-FY2024].

**What the 10-K says drove it:**
- **Data Center revenue grew 217%**, the primary driver of both the top line and the gross margin expansion [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p286].
- Within the Compute & Networking segment, **Compute grew 266%** on higher shipments of the **NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform** for training and inference of LLMs, recommendation engines and generative AI applications; **Networking rose 133%** on higher InfiniBand shipments [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p282].
- Gross margin also benefited from **lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue** — the net effect was an unfavorable 2.7% impact in FY2024 versus 7.5% in FY2023 [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p286].

**Other segments (much smaller contributors):** Gaming +15% on higher sell-in after channel inventory normalized, Professional Visualization +1%, Automotive +21% on self-driving platforms [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p263].

**Note on operating expenses:** They increased on headcount and compensation, but FY2023 had included a $1.4B acquisition termination charge related to the proposed Arm transaction, which flattered the FY2024 comparison [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p263].

**Micron's FY2023 loss (year ended 2023-08-31) was driven by a severe memory-industry downturn — collapsing DRAM and NAND prices — which pushed gross margin negative.**

The numbers [MU-10K-FY2023]:
- Revenue fell 49.5% to $15.54B (from $30.76B in FY2022) [MU-10K-FY2023]
- Gross profit swung to **–$1.416B**, a gross margin of **–9.1%** (from +45.2% in FY2022) [MU-10K-FY2023]
- Operating loss of $5.745B (operating margin –37.0%) and net loss of $5.833B (net margin –37.5%) [MU-10K-FY2023]

According to the 10-K, the causes were [MU-10K-FY2023#p231]:
1. **Declines in average selling prices for both DRAM and NAND** — the primary driver of the margin collapse.
2. **Charges to write inventories down to net realizable value (NRV)** as a result of those price declines [MU-10K-FY2023#p232].
3. **$382 million of facility underutilization costs** in 2023 [MU-10K-FY2023#p231].

The filing's "Industry Conditions" section describes the backdrop: a challenging pricing environment, elevated inventory levels at both suppliers and customers, and a significant supply-demand mismatch. In response, Micron cut capital expenditures and significantly reduced wafer starts for both DRAM and NAND in 2023 [MU-10K-FY2023#p222].

Note that the loss was not attributable to weak demand volumes alone — the 10-K frames it as a pricing/inventory-driven margin problem, with write-downs recorded ahead of when inventory was sold (which lowers cost of goods sold in later periods) [MU-10K-FY2023#p232]. By FY2024 revenue rebounded 61.6% to $25.11B and net income returned to $0.778B [MU-10K-FY2024].

Micron's FY2023 net loss of $5.833 billion (vs. net income of $8.687 billion in FY2022) was driven primarily by an industry downturn and pricing declines, per its 10-K [MU-10K-FY2023].

Management's stated reasons:
- **Industry downturn/demand weakness:** the memory and storage environment "deteriorated sharply" from Q4 2022 through 2023 due to weak end-market demand, macroeconomic challenges, and customer inventory reductions [MU-10K-FY2023#p221].
- **Pricing declines:** revenue fell 49.5% to $15.540 billion; DRAM sales fell 51% on a high-40s percent ASP decline, and NAND sales fell 46% on a low-50s percent ASP decline [MU-10K-FY2023] [MU-10K-FY2023#p230].
- **Inventory write-downs:** $1.83 billion of NRV charges, plus $382 million of facility underutilization costs, drove gross margin from 45.2% to −9.1% [MU-10K-FY2023#p221] [MU-10K-FY2023#p231].
- **Restructuring:** $171 million of charges under the 2023 Restructure Plan (headcount reduction approaching 15%) [MU-10K-FY2023#p384].

Operating loss was $5.745 billion (operating margin −37.0%) [MU-10K-FY2023]. Note: the $435 million Lehi/3D XPoint impairment was a FY2021 charge, not FY2023 [MU-10K-FY2023#p228].

## Micron Technology (MU) — FY2023 net loss: findings

**Fiscal year:** 2022-09-02 to 2023-08-31 [MU-10K-FY2023]

### Key figures (USD billions, FY2023 vs FY2022) [MU-10K-FY2023] / [MU-10K-FY2022]
| Metric | FY2023 | FY2022 |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 15.540 | 30.758 |
| Revenue growth | −49.5% | +11.0% |
| Gross profit | −1.416 | 13.898 |
| Gross margin | −9.1% | 45.2% |
| Operating income (loss) | −5.745 | 9.702 |
| Operating margin | −37.0% | 31.5% |
| Net income (loss) | −5.833 | 8.687 |
| Net margin | −37.5% | 28.2% |
| R&D | 3.114 (20.0% of revenue) | 3.116 (10.1%) |

### Management's stated reasons (10-K)
1. **Industry downturn / demand weakness:** "The memory and storage industry environment deteriorated sharply in the fourth quarter of 2022 and throughout 2023 due to weak demand in many end markets combined with global and macroeconomic challenges and lower demand resulting from customer actions to reduce inventory levels" [MU-10K-FY2023#p221].
2. **Pricing declines → revenue collapse:** Total revenue fell 49% vs 2022; DRAM sales −51% on a "high-40s percent range decline in average selling prices" plus high-single-digit bit shipment declines; NAND sales −46% on a "low-50s percent range decline in average selling prices" [MU-10K-FY2023#p230]. All four business units declined: CNBU −58%, MBU −50%, EBU −31%, SBU −44% [MU-10K-FY2023#p235].
3. **Inventory NRV write-downs:** $1.83 billion of charges in 2023 to write inventories down to estimated net realizable value, driven by ASP declines for both DRAM and NAND [MU-10K-FY2023#p221]. These, plus ASP declines and $382 million of facility underutilization costs, drove gross margin from 45% to negative 9% [MU-10K-FY2023#p231].
4. **Underutilization costs:** $382 million of period costs from fabrication facility underutilization in 2023 due to wafer start reductions; ~$200 million expected in Q1 2024 [MU-10K-FY2023#p223].
5. **Restructuring:** 2023 Restructure Plan (headcount reduction approaching 15% by end of calendar 2023) with $171 million of restructure charges in 2023, primarily employee severance; plan substantially completed in Q3 2023 [MU-10K-FY2023#p384]. SG&A expenses were 14% lower than 2022, and R&D was roughly flat (decreases in employee compensation offset by higher depreciation) [MU-10K-FY2023#p239][MU-10K-FY2023#p240].
6. **Mitigation:** reduced capital expenditures and significantly reduced wafer starts for both DRAM and NAND; no NRV write-downs in Q4 2023 as pricing trends began to improve [MU-10K-FY2023#p222].

Note: the Lehi, Utah fab / 3D XPoint impairment ($435 million) was a FY2021 charge, not FY2023 [MU-10K-FY2023#p228].

## Revenue growth in fiscal year 2024

| Company | FY2024 revenue | Growth vs FY2023 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| NVIDIA | $60.922B | **+125.9%** | [NVDA-10K-FY2024] |
| AMD | $25.785B | **+13.7%** | [AMD-10K-FY2024] |
| Intel | $53.101B | **−2.1%** | [INTC-10K-FY2024] |

Note on periods: NVIDIA's FY2024 ended 2024-01-28, while AMD's and Intel's FY2024 ended 2024-12-28 — so NVIDIA's figure is roughly a year earlier in calendar terms.

## Main reason for the change, per each 10-K

**NVIDIA — +126%, driven overwhelmingly by Data Center / AI.**
Revenue rose to $60.9B, up 126%, with Data Center revenue up 217% [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p262]. Data Center compute revenue was up 244% and networking up 133% [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p262]. The Compute & Networking increase was attributed to "higher shipments of the NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform for the training and inference of LLMs, recommendation engines and generative AI applications," with networking up on higher InfiniBand shipments [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p282]. Gaming rose 15% on higher sell-in after channel inventory normalized, Professional Visualization +1%, Automotive +21% [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p262, #p263].

**AMD — +14%, driven by Data Center and Client, partly offset by Gaming and Embedded.**
Net revenue rose 14% to $25.8B from $22.7B, "driven by the performance of our Data Center and Client segments" [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282]. Data Center revenue of $12.6B was up 94% on higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282, #p307]; Client revenue of $7.1B rose 52% on higher Ryzen mobile and desktop processor sales [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282]. This was partially offset by Gaming revenue falling 58% to $2.6B on lower semi-custom product revenue, and lower Embedded revenue [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282].

**Intel — −2%, driven by non-core/foundry declines that outweighed modest product growth.**
Revenue fell $1.1B, or 2%, to $53.1B "due to lower all other revenue and lower Intel Foundry revenue, partially offset by higher Intel Products revenue" [INTC-10K-FY2024#p98]. All other revenue dropped 32% as Altera customers tempered purchases to reduce inventories and Mobileye revenue fell on EyeQ inventory reduction; Intel Foundry external revenue fell 60% on lower traditional packaging services and equipment sales [INTC-10K-FY2024#p98]. Intel Products revenue rose 3%: CCG +4% on notebook volume up 12% (partly offset by lower desktop demand and the exit of legacy businesses), and DCAI +1% on higher server ASPs (+12%) despite server volume down 10% [INTC-10K-FY2024#p98, #p130].

**NVIDIA (FY2024 ended Jan 2024):** Revenue rose from $26.974B to $60.922B, **+125.9%** [NVDA-10K-FY2024]. Main reason per the 10-K: Data Center revenue up 217% (compute +244%, networking +133%), driven by strong demand for the NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform for LLM training/inference, recommendation engines and generative AI, plus higher InfiniBand shipments [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p262, #p282].

**AMD (FY2024 ended Dec 2024):** Revenue rose from $22.68B to $25.785B, **+13.7%** [AMD-10K-FY2024]. Main reason per the 10-K: growth "driven by the performance of our Data Center and Client segments" — Data Center +94% to $12.6B (AMD Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs) and Client +52% to $7.1B (Ryzen mobile/desktop), partially offset by Gaming −58% and lower Embedded revenue [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282].

**Intel (FY2024 ended Dec 2024):** Revenue fell from $54.228B to $53.101B, **−2.1%** [INTC-10K-FY2024]. Main reason per the 10-K: lower "all other" revenue (Altera and Mobileye inventory reductions) and lower Intel Foundry external revenue (−60%), partially offset by higher Intel Products revenue (+3%) [INTC-10K-FY2024#p157, #p130].

findings.answer:
**NVIDIA CORP (NVDA) — FY2024 (year ended 2024-01-28)**

**Revenue:**
- FY2023 (ended 2023-01-29): $26.974B [NVDA-10K-FY2023]
- FY2024 (ended 2024-01-28): $60.922B [NVDA-10K-FY2024]
- YoY revenue growth FY2024: **+125.9%** (server-derived metric) [NVDA-10K-FY2024]

**Main reason for the change (per 10-K):**
- Revenue for FY2024 was $60.9B, up 126% from a year ago; **Data Center revenue was up 217%**, Data Center compute revenue up 244% and networking revenue up 133% [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p262].
- Strong demand driven by enterprise software and consumer internet applications, and multiple industry verticals including automotive, financial services, and healthcare; customers access NVIDIA AI infrastructure both via cloud and on-premises [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p262].
- Compute & Networking segment revenue grew 266% on higher shipments of the **NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform** for training and inference of LLMs, recommendation engines and generative AI applications; networking up 133% on higher InfiniBand shipments [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p282].
- Other segments: Gaming +15% (higher sell-in after channel inventory normalization), ProViz +1%, Automotive +21% (self-driving platforms) [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p262, #p263].
- Gross margin increased, primarily driven by Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p263].

Note: FY2023 also included a $1.4B Arm acquisition termination charge, which affects operating income comparisons but not revenue [NVDA-10K-FY2024#p263].

findings.answer:
**AMD — FY2024 revenue growth and 10-K explanation**

**Revenue (USD billions):**
- FY2023 (period 2023-01-01..2023-12-30): $22.68B [AMD-10K-FY2023]
- FY2024 (period 2023-12-31..2024-12-28): $25.785B [AMD-10K-FY2024]
- YoY revenue growth FY2024: **+13.7%** (server-computed) [AMD-10K-FY2024]; FY2023 had been −3.9% [AMD-10K-FY2023]

**Main reasons per the FY2024 10-K** [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282]:
- Net revenue rose 14% to $25.8B from $22.7B, "driven by the performance of our Data Center and Client segments."
- **Data Center**: $12.6B, +94% vs $6.5B in 2023, driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct™ GPUs and AMD EPYC™ CPUs [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282; AMD-10K-FY2024#p307]. Data Center operating income rose to $3.5B from $1.3B on higher revenue, partly offset by higher R&D [AMD-10K-FY2024#p307].
- **Client**: $7.1B, +52% vs $4.7B, primarily higher sales of AMD Ryzen™ mobile and desktop processors [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282].
- **Partially offset by declines**: Gaming net revenue $2.6B, −58% vs $6.2B, primarily lower semi-custom product revenue; Embedded net revenue $3.6B (also down) [AMD-10K-FY2024#p282].
- Gross margin rose to 49% from 46% on a favorable revenue mix shift toward higher Data Center and Client revenue and lower Gaming revenue, partly offset by lower Embedded revenue [AMD-10K-FY2024#p312].

findings.task: For Intel Corporation (ticker INTC), fiscal year 2024 (fiscal year ends 12-27, so FY2024 ended in December 2024): find total revenue for fiscal years 2023 and 2024 using get_financials, compute the year-over-year revenue growth rate for fiscal year 2024, and use search_filing to find the main reason(s) Intel's 10-K gives for the change in revenue in fiscal year 2024.
findings.answer:
## Intel (INTC) — FY2024 revenue growth

**Revenue (USD billions):**
- FY2023: $54.228B [INTC-10K-FY2023]
- FY2024: $53.101B [INTC-10K-FY2024]
- **FY2024 revenue growth: −2.1%** (server-computed `revenue_growth`) [INTC-10K-FY2024]

Note: FY2024 period is 2023-12-31..2024-12-28; FY2023 period is 2023-01-01..2023-12-30.

**Main reasons for the change per the 10-K (Consolidated Revenue Walk):**
"2024 revenue was $53.1 billion, down $1.1 billion, or 2%, from 2023 due to lower all other revenue and lower Intel Foundry revenue, partially offset by higher Intel Products revenue." [INTC-10K-FY2024#p157]

- **All other revenue** (Altera + Mobileye + startups) fell 32% to $3.8B, down $1.8B: Altera revenue $1.5B, down $1.3B, as "customers tempered purchases to reduce existing inventories across all product lines"; Mobileye revenue $1.7B, down $425M, as customers reduced existing inventories of EyeQ products [INTC-10K-FY2024#p157][INTC-10K-FY2024#p154]
- **Intel Foundry external revenue** decreased 60% from 2023 "due to lower traditional packaging services and lower equipment sales" [INTC-10K-FY2024#p157]
- **Offset — Intel Products revenue** rose 3% to $48.9B, up $1.3B [INTC-10K-FY2024#p130]:
  - CCG +$1.0B (+4%): notebook revenue $19.1B, up $2.1B, on 12% higher notebook volume as customer inventory levels improved; desktop revenue $9.7B, down $516M on 5% lower volume; other CCG down $530M on exit of legacy businesses [INTC-10K-FY2024#p130]
  - DCAI +$182M (+1%): server ASPs +12% on higher mix of high core count products, server volume −10% [INTC-10K-FY2024#p130][INTC-10K-FY2024#p158]

**Bottom line:** Intel's FY2024 revenue declined 2.1% to $53.1B, driven mainly by a 32% drop in "all other" revenue (Altera and Mobileye inventory corrections) and a 60% drop in Intel Foundry external revenue, partly offset by 3% growth in Intel Products (notebook-led CCG and modest DCAI growth).

answer:
Among the software companies reviewed, **ServiceNow (NOW)** had the lowest FY2024 operating margin at **12.4%** ($1.364B operating income on $10.984B revenue) [NOW-10K-FY2024]. (Salesforce was next at 14.4% [CRM-10K-FY2024]; Cisco 22.6% [CSCO-10K-FY2024]; Adobe 31.3% [ADBE-10K-FY2024]; Microsoft 44.6% [MSFT-10K-FY2024].)

Per its FY2024 10-K, the main drivers of ServiceNow's operating expense increase were:
- **Sales & marketing: +$553M** — higher headcount/personnel costs incl. stock-based comp and overhead (+$330M), amortization of deferred commissions +$90M, and other program expenses (branding, advertising, events) +$95M [NOW-10K-FY2024#p271, #p272]
- **R&D: +$419M** — primarily increased headcount and personnel-related costs [NOW-10K-FY2024#p272]
- **G&A: +$73M** — higher personnel costs ex-SBC (+$37M) and other corporate/outside services (+$67M), partly offset by a $36M SBC decrease [NOW-10K-FY2024#p275]

Note: the question's premise that the lowest-margin company would report an *increase* in operating expenses holds for ServiceNow, but not universally — Salesforce's opex actually *decreased* in FY2024 [CRM-10K-FY2024#p329].
